payload.title: The merge_intent row is still published before every lane merge but nothing reads it since _aria_merged_prs was deleted, so a lane merge whose merged rows never reached the store is invisible to self-revert unless its PR has a plan in IMPLEMENTATION_RECORDED, and two docstrings still state the retired rule
evidence: aria-kernel/aria_kernel/merge_authority.py:609-632 (the intent docstring: an intent whose PR later merged at that head is an ARIA merge (self_revert))
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/merge_authority.py:353-364 (the intent publish is still a gate before every merge call)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/own_pr_ci.py:50-59 (is_own_pr_head docstring: a merge_intent could never be tied to its merge)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/merge_record.py:396-405 (arias_merges reads the merged rows only, never an intent)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/self_revert.py:674-677 (a PR absent from arias_merges is skipped as not_an_aria_merge)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/self_revert.py:1513-1519 (revert_landed needs the revert PR in arias_merges)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/implementation_reconciler.py:163-182 (the one recovery left: _observe_merge, only for plans in IMPLEMENTATION_RECORDED)
payload.rule_violated: ARIA-HIGH-222: a merge can never be invisible to self-revert; F3.3a one-owner rule (merge_record.py 358-364): merge_record is the one reader of which merges are ARIA's, so its record must be complete for every merge the lane makes.
payload.notes: The lane publishes a merge_intent at head H, merges, and loses its final publish (runner death or a lost fast-forward race), so no merged row exists. A self-revert PR, or any lane-merged ARIA PR with no plan in IMPLEMENTATION_RECORDED, is then absent from arias_merges: a red outcome on it is skipped as not_an_aria_merge, and its revert_landed row and rollback_success event are never written, where the pre-F3.4 reader recovered it from the intent. The review's probe gave no decision on the branch and revert_opened at the merge-base. The intent publish stays a gate before every merge call and costs a publish round trip for no reader. Close condition: Either restore the recovery in the one owner (merge_record reconciles an unsettled merge_intent whose PR GitHub reports merged at that head into a merged row, as reconcile_enqueued_merges does for the queue) with a test that a lost merged row is recovered for a non-plan PR, or retire the intent publish and correct both docstrings in the same change. Verified at origin/main ae2958653d.
